newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA CITY TO HELP PRIVATE FIRMS EXPAND ABROAD.
newsitem.headline: CHINA CITY TO HELP PRIVATE FIRMS EXPAND ABROAD.

text.p: China's booming southern city of Guangzhou is considering introducing regulations to encourage local private enterprises to open overseas subsidiaries under state supervision, a local trade official said on Thursday.

Guangzhou, the capital of Guangdong province, was the first Chinese city to consider such a system for guiding private overseas investment, said the official of the city's Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Commission.
Under the proposed system, private firms operating overseas would be under state administration and would be eligible for assistance from Chinese embassies and commercial chambers, he said.
It was not clear when the regulations, which had been proposed by local trade and business officials, would be formally issued, he said but declined to give further details.

The official Xinhua news agency said all registered private enterprises in Guangzhou would be allowed to open solely funded, joint venture, cooperative or shareholding overseas subsidiaries so long as the new ventures earned foreign exchange and imported advanced equipment or scarce raw materials or products.

Private overseas companies investing in their parent companies or other enterprises in Guangzhou would enjoy the same preferential government treatment granted to foreign companies, it said but did not elaborate.
